title: Record the constant 3 on the longer reservoir layout (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped comparison. No new κ. The selected conditional exponent stays `60403/20000000`, and PR #4100 is not accepted.

PR #4646 reaches `r (2/B + β) ≤ p 2^{-G} / 6400` when `L ≤ p`. On the admitted layout `p = 2`, `ell = 2`, `L = 65536`, `G = 256`, and `r = r_max = 2`, the exact sharp ratio is

```text
C_* = 2 + 2^{-15871} - 2^{-16126}.
```

This is the `C` in `r (2/B + β) = C p 2^{-G}`. It lies strictly between 2 and 3, so `C = 2` fails and `C = 3` holds. The integer 3 replaces `1/6400` for this one inequality.

The published window term has exact ratio `2 + 2^{-15869}` and the same integer threshold. The production plan `r_max = 5`, `p = 9240576` still satisfies `5 · 3 · 6400 ≤ p`, so `1/6400` is not retuned there.

## Task and overlap

- Base: canonical main `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`, fetched 2026-10-22T23:47:42Z, priority revision 7.
- Card: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope **refined**. This is the open question of PR #4913.
- Predecessor: PR #4174 admits the layout. PR #4646 supplies the `1/6400` line. PR #4328 supplies the `L ≤ p` hypothesis.
- Package: `research/crt-reservoir-length-constant/`.
- Overlap at 2026-10-22T23:47:39Z: this package, PR #4913's open question, and the original `1/6400` proof. No other evaluation of this ratio.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/crt-reservoir-length-constant
```

Observed `PASS_CRT_RESERVOIR_LENGTH_CONSTANT layout_p=2 layout_L=65536 r=2 G=256 sharp_between=2,3 integer_C=3`, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/crt-reservoir-length-constant outcome=completed`.

Not run: the 104,864-plan census, the repair tariff, the `E` product, Lean, and Docker.

## Open next questions

1. For every layout the #4174 constructor accepts, is `C = 3 r_max / p` sufficient at `r = r_max`? First step: show that every accepted layout has `G ≥ 256`, so `2 + 2^{1-62G} < 3`.
